pack.name: Cronsole Native
pack.description: Jobs Cronsole schedules and runs itself — no agent, no Task Scheduler entry. Programs and scripts on the Cronsole host, plus HTTP uptime checks and heartbeats.

templates.name: Run a Program (Cronsole)
templates.description: Run any executable with arguments on the machine hosting Cronsole — no agent, no Task Scheduler entry. Cronsole schedules and runs it itself.

parameters.label: Executable path
parameters.help: Absolute path to the program, as seen by the machine running the Cronsole backend. On a Dockerized stack that is the container, not your desktop.

templates.name: Node Script (Cronsole)
templates.description: Run a Node.js script on the Cronsole host on a schedule.

parameters.label: Script file path
parameters.help: Absolute path to the .js/.mjs file on the machine running the Cronsole backend.

templates.name: Python Script (Cronsole)
templates.description: Run a Python script on the Cronsole host on a schedule.

parameters.label: Script file path
parameters.help: Absolute path to the .py file on the machine running the Cronsole backend. `python` must be on that machine’s PATH.

templates.name: Keep a Repo Fresh (Cronsole)
templates.description: Pull the latest commits into a local repository on the Cronsole host — the agent-free version of Git Sync.

parameters.label: Repository path
parameters.help: Absolute path to the repository on the machine running the Cronsole backend. `--ff-only` refuses rather than creating a merge nobody reviewed.

templates.name: Uptime Check (Cronsole)
templates.description: Call a URL every few minutes and record whether it answered. Runs in Cronsole itself — no agent, and it works on a machine with no Task Scheduler.

parameters.label: URL
parameters.help: The endpoint to GET. A non-2xx response is recorded as a failed run, which is what makes this a check rather than a ping.

templates.name: Monitor Heartbeat (Cronsole)
templates.description: Ping a dead-man’s-switch URL (Healthchecks.io, Better Stack, Cronitor) on a schedule so an outside monitor notices when Cronsole itself stops.

parameters.label: URL
parameters.help: The heartbeat URL your monitor gave you. It alerts when the ping stops — which is the one failure a scheduler cannot report about itself.

templates.name: Write a Script (Cronsole)
templates.description: A starting point for a scheduled script you write in Cronsole itself. Nothing needs to exist on disk — the body is stored with the task and runs under the interpreter you pick.

templates.name: PowerShell Disk Report (Cronsole)
templates.description: Print free space for every fixed drive on the Cronsole host, so the numbers land in the run history and you can read them back over time.

action.body:
# Needs PowerShell on the machine running the Cronsole backend.
# That is your desktop for a normal install, and the CONTAINER on a
# Dockerized stack — where these drives are the container’s, not yours.

Get-CimInstance Win32_LogicalDisk -Filter "DriveType=3" |
  ForEach-Object {
    $freeGb  = [math]::Round($_.FreeSpace / 1GB, 1)
    $totalGb = [math]::Round($_.Size / 1GB, 1)
    "{0} {1} GB free of {2} GB" -f $_.DeviceID, $freeGb, $totalGb
  }

templates.name: Endpoint Health Check (Cronsole)
templates.description: Call a URL and require the response to actually say it is healthy — not just return 200. A failure here is a fact about your system, so it is worth alerting on.

parameters.label: URL
parameters.help: The health endpoint to call, e.g. https://example.com/healthz.

parameters.label: Response must contain
parameters.help: Text that must appear in the response body. This is what makes it a health check rather than a ping — a 200 without this fails.

templates.name: Backup Freshness Check (Cronsole)
templates.description: Fail if a backup file has not been written recently — the dead-man switch for a job that stopped silently. A missing file fails too.

parameters.label: File to watch
parameters.help: Path as seen by the machine running the Cronsole backend — the container on a Dockerized stack, not your desktop. A path that is only valid on your PC will report the file as missing.

parameters.label: Fail if older than (minutes)
parameters.help: Default is 24 hours, which suits a nightly backup. Leave headroom for the job to finish.

templates.name: Disk Space Check (Cronsole)
templates.description: Fail when free space on a volume drops below your floor, so you hear about it before something else fails for a reason that looks unrelated.

parameters.label: Path on the volume
parameters.help: Any path on the volume to measure, as seen by the machine running the Cronsole backend.

parameters.label: Minimum free space (bytes)
parameters.help: Default is 10 GB. In bytes, because that is what the check stores — 1 GB is 1073741824.

templates.name: Port Reachable Check (Cronsole)
templates.description: Confirm something still accepts connections on a host and port — a database, a broker, an internal service with no HTTP endpoint to call.

parameters.label: Host
parameters.help: Resolved from the machine running the Cronsole backend, so an internal name has to be reachable from there.

parameters.label: Port
parameters.help: The check succeeds if a TCP connection is accepted within 15 seconds. It does not log in or send anything.
